messages:
maya: seeing apiserver 5xx spike in us-west1, controllers timing out when trying to attach GPUs. anyone else?
ops-bot: [ALERT] apiserver error_rate increased to 6.8% in us-west1 - check: /clusters/us-west1/controlplane
sam: saw ~80k SNAT entries on the region NAT gateways, seemed to coincide with a burst of provisioning calls
lee: GPU attach pods are stuck in ContainerCreating with `rpc error: code = Unavailable` to attach daemon
jordan: logs from apiserver proxy: "dial tcp <agent>: connect: connection refused" then long retries, latency to kubelet-star > 2s
maya: repro gist: https://short.url/attach-logs - shows backoff loop from controller-manager
tariq: quick metric — controller-manager leader election churned twice in last 3m, leader lock renewals failing at 1.2s
sam: hypothesis: mesh egress (service-mesh sidecars) are fanouting controlplane calls -> NAT conntrack exhaustion -> apiserver upstream flakiness -> controller timeouts
lee: rolling kube-proxy doesn't help if NAT is exhausted. we can try bypassing mesh egress for controlplane IPs or pod CIDRs
maya: can we patch NetworkPolicy to allow direct egress from nodes to apiserver IPs? also consider pinning kubelet to 0.10s keepalive
jordan: ops-bot applied automute for some noisy diagnostics earlier; re-enabling verbose logs would add 2x more egress, avoid for now :grimacing:
sam: mitigation path I'd try now: 1) add egress-exempt annotation on controller-manager and attach workers to skip sidecar 2) increase NAT ephemeral ports (provider request) 3) scale apiserver horizontally to absorb retries
tariq: provider already rate-limited NAT increases; raising NAT might take ~30m. do step 1 immediately. I can push a small k8s patch
lee: will that break service-mesh expectations? need to update sidecar injection template to skip controlplane IPs
maya: patch applied: `sidecar.istio.io/inject: 'false'` on controllers and attach-daemonset pods in us-west1.
sam: seeing immediate drop in SNAT growth rate. conntrack now 20% lower
ops-bot: [DEPLOY] patch maya/skip-mesh-exempt applied to us-west1 controllers by tariq
jordan: apiserver 5xx rate down to 1.1% and controller-manager leader stable again
tariq: still seeing some attach retries from older pods. recommend rolling attach-daemonset to pick up annotation and then drain small batches
maya: agree. start rolling 10% at a time, monitor attach error rate and token costs
sam: followup: long-term we should route controlplane egress via a dedicated NAT pool or VPC egress gateway, and throttle sidecar fanout for controlplane endpoints
lee: +1 on dedicated egress. also recommend an internal fallback: if GPU attach RPCs fail X times, fallback to pre-provisioned warm pool to avoid thundering
jordan: I'll open infra ticket with priority-high for NAT pool and warm-pool design
maya: thanks all. will keep thread updated during rollout. :thumbsup:
sam: one more note — cost spike from retries visible in token-metering; tagging for finance FYI
maya: tagged @finance for visibility in the ticket
jordan: closing loop: apiserver latency back to baseline after rollouts. keep monitoring for 1h
ops-bot: [RESOLVED] Alert cleared for apiserver error_rate in us-west1
maya: awesome work, great quick mitigation. we'll create RFC for egress gateway + warm gpu pool
